I played a game of chess with my uncle.
For lunch, my dad cooked kabsa for the whole family.
After lunch I relaxed on the sofa with a cold drink.

dialogue.t: How was your weekend?
It was quiet. We stayed at home.
What happened on Friday?
We watched a film about the ocean.
And on Saturday?
My dad cooked kabsa, and I played a game of chess.

grammar.title: Past simple: regular verbs + -ed
grammar.ar: للحديث عن شيء حدث وانتهى نضيف ed للفعل: play ← played، watch ← watched. الفعل نفسه لكل الأشخاص.
examples: I played a game with my sister.
We watched a film on Friday.
My mum cooked rice and chicken.

words.ex: Last Friday we visited my grandparents in Qassim.
Last weekend I visited my aunt and her new baby.
I helped my grandpa with his garden.
Grandma baked a date cake for us.
My mum and my aunt chatted for hours.
We laughed a lot at my uncle's funny jokes.

dialogue.t: What did you do last weekend?
We visited my grandparents on their farm.
What happened there?
I helped my grandpa with the palm trees.
And your grandma?
She baked a date cake, and we chatted in the garden.
That sounds lovely!

grammar.title: Spelling: -d, -ied and double letters
grammar.ar: إذا انتهى الفعل بـ e نضيف d فقط: bake ← baked. وإذا انتهى بحرف ساكن ثم y نحوّلها إلى ied: carry ← carried. وبعض الأفعال القصيرة نضاعف آخر حرف: chat ← chatted.
examples: Grandma baked a cake.
I carried the dates to the car.
We chatted in the garden.

words.ex: Yesterday at school we started a new science project.
Our class started a project about the moon.
In art class Reem painted a picture of the desert at sunset.
We practised our song for the school show.
I finished my maths homework in the library.
At break we chatted about the football match.

dialogue.t: How was school yesterday?
Busy! We started a project about the planets.
What happened in art class?
I painted a picture of Saturn.
And in PE?
We practised for Sports Day.

grammar.title: Time words: yesterday, this morning, last …
grammar.ar: نستخدم كلمات الزمن مع الماضي: yesterday (أمس)، this morning (هذا الصباح)، last week (الأسبوع الماضي). نضعها في أول الجملة أو آخرها.
examples: Yesterday we practised for Sports Day.
I finished my project this morning.
Our class started a new book last week.

words.ex: Two days ago our team played against Class 5B.
Yesterday I watched a match between Al Hilal and Al Nassr.
Omar passed the ball to me, and I kicked it hard.
Salem scored a goal in the first five minutes.
He kicked hard but missed the goal.
Everyone cheered when the match ended.

dialogue.t: How was the match?
Great! Two days ago we played against Class 5B.
What happened?
I passed the ball to Ali, but he missed.
Oh no!
Then he scored a goal, and everyone cheered!

grammar.title: Time words: ago and last
grammar.ar: نستخدم ago بعد المدة: two days ago (قبل يومين). ونستخدم last قبل الزمن: last Thursday (الخميس الماضي). لا نقول the last week.
examples: We played a match two days ago.
Last Thursday I scored a goal.
My team practised three weeks ago.

words.ex: I tidied my room before my cousins arrived.
After dinner, I washed the dishes with my sister.
I carried the shopping bags to the kitchen.
Faisal emptied the bin in the kitchen every evening.
I helped my dad with the car.
We cleaned the car. After that, we watched TV.

dialogue.t: Was your weekend busy?
Yes! Our aunts visited us, so I helped my mum.
What did you do?
First, I tidied my room.
And after that?
After that, I washed the dishes and carried the coffee.

grammar.title: First … After that …
grammar.ar: لترتيب الأحداث نستخدم First (أولاً) ثم After that (بعد ذلك). نضع فاصلة بعدهما.
examples: First, I tidied my room.
After that, I emptied the bin.
First, we cooked lunch. After that, we washed the dishes.

words.ex: First, we visited my uncle.
Then we walked in the park.
After that, my family cooked dinner together.
Finally, I had a shower and relaxed.
We really enjoyed the cool evening in the park.
On Saturday we visited the new science museum.

dialogue.t: Tell me about your weekend.
First, we stayed at home and played board games.
And then?
Then the rain stopped, and we walked in the park.
What about Saturday?
We visited my aunt. Finally, we watched the stars. I really enjoyed it!

grammar.title: Telling a story in order
grammar.ar: نحكي القصة بالترتيب: First (أولاً) ← Then (ثم) ← After that (بعد ذلك) ← Finally (أخيراً)، مع أفعال ماضية.
examples: First, we visited my aunt.
Then we walked to the park. After that, we played football.
Finally, we returned home and relaxed.

words.ex: Last summer we went to the beach in Jeddah.
I swam in the sea for an hour.
We had a picnic on the beach with sandwiches and juice.
My sister and I built a sandcastle near the water.
On the beach I found a beautiful white shell.
We came back home at nine o'clock, very tired.

dialogue.t: Where did you go last weekend?
We went to the beach in Jeddah.
Did you swim in the sea?
Yes, I did. The water was warm.
Did you build a sandcastle?
Yes! My sister and I built a huge one.

grammar.title: Past simple: irregular verbs
grammar.ar: بعض الأفعال لا نضيف لها ed بل تتغيّر كلها في الماضي، ونحفظها: go ← went، swim ← swam، build ← built، find ← found، come ← came.
examples: We went to the beach.
I swam in the sea.
My brother found a shell.

words.ex: Last winter we went to the desert near Riyadh.
My uncle drove us to the sand dunes.
My little brother rode a camel for the first time.
We made a campfire and cooked dinner on it.
At night we saw hundreds of stars.
We slept in a big tent near the sand dunes.

dialogue.t: Did you go camping last weekend?
Yes, I did. We went to the desert.
What did you do there?
I rode a camel, and we made a campfire.
Where did you sleep?
We slept in a tent and saw hundreds of stars.

grammar.title: Did you …? Yes, I did. / No, I didn't.
grammar.ar: للسؤال عن الماضي: Did + الفاعل + الفعل في صورته الأساسية. نقول Did you ride? ولا نقول Did you rode? والجواب القصير: Yes, I did. / No, I didn't.
examples: Did you ride a camel? — Yes, I did.
Did you sleep in a tent? — No, I didn't.
Did your dad drive? — Yes, he did.

words.ex: At the museum we saw an old map of Arabia.
I took photos of the old swords.
We learnt about the history of Riyadh.
Our guide showed us a big rock from space.
We saw ancient writing on a big stone.
At the museum shop I bought a souvenir for my sister.

dialogue.t: What did you see at the museum?
We saw ancient writing on big stones.
Did you take photos?
Yes, lots! I took photos of the old swords.
What did you buy?
I bought a souvenir for my brother.

grammar.title: What / Where did …?
grammar.ar: نضع كلمة السؤال قبل did: What did you see? Where did you go? والفعل بعد did يبقى في صورته الأساسية (see وليس saw).
examples: What did you see? — We saw old maps.
Where did you buy it? — At the museum shop.
What did you learn about? — The history of Riyadh.

words.ex: Last spring we flew from Riyadh to AlUla.
We went to Abha by car. It took ten hours.
We stayed at a hotel in the desert for three nights.
On the trip we met a family from Italy.
The view from the mountain was amazing.
In AlUla I took photos of the huge rocks.

dialogue.t: How did you get to AlUla?
We flew from Jeddah.
Where did you stay?
We stayed at a small hotel for three nights.
Who did you meet there?
We met a family from Spain.

grammar.title: How / Who / How long …?
grammar.ar: How did you get there? للسؤال عن وسيلة السفر، وWho did you meet? للسؤال عن الأشخاص، وHow long did you stay? للسؤال عن المدة.
examples: How did you get there? — By plane.
Who did you meet? — A family from Spain.
How long did you stay? — Three nights.

words.ex: We had fun at Boulevard World last night.
My favourite ride was the big wheel.
We got tickets for the show online.
For dinner we ate burgers and fresh juice.
The park was very crowded on Thursday night.
At the shop I bought a toy falcon.

dialogue.t: Did you go to Riyadh Season?
Yes, we went on Thursday night.
Was it crowded?
Very crowded, but we had fun!
What did you eat?
We ate noodles and ice cream.

grammar.title: Was it …? / Were they …?
grammar.ar: للسؤال عن الوصف في الماضي نستخدم Was / Were بدون did: Was it crowded? Were the rides fun? والجواب: Yes, it was. / No, they weren't.
examples: Was it crowded? — Yes, it was.
Were the rides fun? — Yes, they were.
Was the food good? — No, it wasn't.

words.ex: Where did you go last summer? — To Abha.
How did you get to Abha? — By car.
Who did you go to the beach with? — My cousins.
What did you do in Jeddah? — We swam and fished.
We had fun when we rode the cable car.
We came back from Abha after a week.

dialogue.t: Where did you go in the holidays?
I went to Abha.
How did you get there?
By car, with my family.
What did you do there?
We rode the cable car and had a picnic. We had fun!

grammar.title: Question words: Where, How, Who, What, When
grammar.ar: مراجعة كلمات السؤال في الماضي: كلمة السؤال + did + الفاعل + الفعل الأساسي. Where (أين) – How (كيف) – Who (من) – What (ماذا) – When (متى).
examples: Where did you go? — To Abha.
When did you come back? — After a week.
Who did you go with? — With my family.

words.ex: A cheetah is faster than a horse.
An elephant is stronger than a lion.
A whale is heavier than an elephant.
A shark is more dangerous than a dolphin.
The peregrine falcon is the fastest bird in the world.
My grandpa has a falcon called Saqr.

dialogue.t: Which is faster, a cheetah or a horse?
A cheetah is faster than a horse.
What's the fastest animal in the world?
The falcon!
Which is stronger, a lion or an elephant?
An elephant is stronger than a lion, and heavier too.

grammar.title: Comparatives: -er than
grammar.ar: للمقارنة بين شيئين نضيف er للصفة القصيرة ثم than: fast ← faster than، strong ← stronger than. وإذا انتهت الصفة بـ y نحوّلها إلى ier: heavy ← heavier.
examples: A cheetah is faster than a horse.
An elephant is stronger than a lion.
A whale is heavier than an elephant.

words.ex: Riyadh is bigger than Abha.
In summer, Riyadh is hotter than Taif.
The city centre is busier than our street.
I think Abha is more beautiful than Riyadh in summer.
Riyadh is the biggest city in Saudi Arabia.
The fastest way to get from Makkah to Madinah is by train.

dialogue.t: Is Riyadh the biggest city in Saudi Arabia?
Yes. It's bigger than Jeddah and busier too.
Which city is cooler in summer?
Abha. It's cooler than Riyadh.
What's the fastest way to get there?
By plane.

grammar.title: Spelling: bigger, hotter, busier
grammar.ar: إذا كانت الصفة قصيرة وتنتهي بحرف علّة واحد ثم حرف ساكن نضاعف الحرف الأخير: big ← bigger، hot ← hotter. وإذا انتهت بـ y نحوّلها إلى ier: busy ← busier.
examples: Riyadh is bigger than Abha.
July is hotter than March.
The mall is busier than the park.

words.ex: I think football is more exciting than golf.
Swimming is easier than running for me.
Tennis is harder than badminton because the ball is fast.
I'm better at volleyball than basketball.
The most popular sport at my school is football.
Basketball is faster than volleyball.

dialogue.t: What about football for Sports Day?
It's the most popular sport, but it's long.
Basketball is more exciting than football.
Yes, but it's harder.
Volleyball is easier than basketball.
Good! I'm better at volleyball.

grammar.title: more … than / better than
grammar.ar: مع الصفات الطويلة نستخدم more … than: exciting ← more exciting than. والصفة good لها شكل خاص: good ← better، وbad ← worse.
examples: Football is more exciting than golf.
I'm better at swimming than running.
My first game was worse than my second game.

words.ex: The Burj Khalifa is taller than the Kingdom Centre.
The Burj Khalifa is the tallest building in the world.
Masmak Fort is older than the Kingdom Centre.
The most famous building in Paris is the Eiffel Tower.
From the top of the tower, you can see the whole city.
The biggest building I visited was a huge mall in Riyadh.

dialogue.t: Is the Kingdom Centre very tall?
Yes, but the Burj Khalifa is taller.
Is it the tallest building in the world?
Yes, it is!
Which is older, Masmak Fort or the Kingdom Centre?
Masmak Fort is older.

grammar.title: Superlatives: the -est / the most …
grammar.ar: للمقارنة بين أكثر من شيئين نستخدم صيغة التفضيل مع the: tall ← the tallest، old ← the oldest، famous ← the most famous.
examples: The Burj Khalifa is the tallest building in the world.
The pyramids are the oldest buildings on our list.
The Eiffel Tower is the most famous building in Paris.

words.ex: The puzzle is cheaper than the doll.
The red bike is more expensive than the blue one.
This school bag is lighter than my old one.
The old phone is worse than the new one because the battery is weak.
The cheapest bike in the shop is 400 riyals.
The blue bike is better than the green one because it has good brakes.

dialogue.t: This red bike is lighter than my old one.
Yes, but it's more expensive than the blue one.
Which one is the cheapest?
The green one, but its brakes are worse.
The blue one is better than the green one.
And it's cheaper than the red one!

grammar.title: good – better – the best / bad – worse – the worst
grammar.ar: بعض الصفات لها أشكال خاصة: good ← better ← the best، وbad ← worse ← the worst. لا نقول gooder أو badder.
examples: The blue bike is better than the green one.
This is the best bike in the shop.
The weather today is worse than yesterday.

words.ex: The best day this year was Sports Day.
The worst day of my week is Monday because I have two tests.
The funniest person in my family is my uncle Saad.
The most interesting lesson this year was about volcanoes.
The most popular game in our class is football.
The longest trip I took was to Tabuk by car.

dialogue.t: Who's the funniest person in the class?
Khalid! His jokes are the funniest.
What was the most interesting trip?
The museum trip. It was more interesting than the zoo trip.
And the worst thing this year?
The longest maths test!

grammar.title: Comparatives and superlatives together
grammar.ar: نستخدم المقارنة (er / more) بين شيئين، والتفضيل (the -est / the most) بين ثلاثة أشياء أو أكثر.
examples: Omar is funny. Khalid is funnier. Salem is the funniest.
This test is long. That test is longer. The maths test is the longest.
Art is interesting. Science is more interesting. The museum trip was the most interesting.

words.ex: Eggs, bread and fruit are a healthy breakfast.
You shouldn't skip breakfast before school.
My favourite fresh fruit is mango.
Fizzy drinks are very sugary.
I feel full of energy after a good breakfast.
You should eat an egg and some fruit for breakfast.

dialogue.t: You look tired. Are you OK?
I skipped breakfast this morning.
You shouldn't skip breakfast.
I only had a chocolate bar.
That's very sugary. You should eat eggs and fresh fruit.
OK, thanks!

grammar.title: should / shouldn't
grammar.ar: نستخدم should + الفعل الأساسي لنعطي نصيحة (من الأفضل أن)، وshouldn't لنقول إن الشيء ليس فكرة جيدة. لا نضع to بعد should.
examples: You should eat fresh fruit.
You shouldn't skip breakfast.
He should drink milk, not fizzy drinks.

words.ex: What's the matter, Omar? You look sad.
When I have a cold, I stay at home and rest.
For a sore throat, you should drink warm water with honey.
You should get some rest and stay in bed.
My favourite warm drink is ginger tea.
You should see a doctor because you have a high temperature.

dialogue.t: What's the matter?
I've got a cold and a sore throat.
You should get some rest.
What should I drink?
You should have a warm drink, like tea with honey.
Thanks!

grammar.title: What's the matter? + advice
grammar.ar: نسأل عن المشكلة بـ What's the matter? والجواب I've got a cold / a sore throat. ثم نعطي النصيحة بـ You should أو You shouldn't.
examples: What's the matter? — I've got a cold.
You should get some rest.
You shouldn't go out in the rain.

words.ex: On school nights, I go to bed early, at nine o'clock.
At the weekend I sometimes stay up late and watch a film.
My screen time every day is about two hours.
I feel tired when I stay up late.
After a good night's sleep, I feel happy and ready for school.
After school, I get some rest by reading on the sofa.

dialogue.t: Why are you so tired?
I stayed up late. I played games until midnight.
You shouldn't stay up late on school nights.
Should I use my tablet in bed?
No, you shouldn't. You should read a book.
OK. Tonight I can go to bed early.

grammar.title: Should I …? Yes, you should. / No, you shouldn't.
grammar.ar: لطلب النصيحة نسأل: Should I + الفعل الأساسي؟ والجواب القصير: Yes, you should. / No, you shouldn't.
examples: Should I go to bed early? — Yes, you should.
Should I use my phone in bed? — No, you shouldn't.
Should we turn off the TV? — Yes, you should.

words.ex: On hot days, I drink plenty of water when I play outside.
I feel thirsty after football practice.
We had lunch in the shade of a big tree.
You should wear a cap when you walk in the sun.
You should put on sun cream before you go to the beach.
On hot days, cold water is better than sugary drinks.

dialogue.t: Let's play football now!
It's midday. We shouldn't play outside now.
When should we play?
In the evening. And you should wear a cap.
What should I take?
You should take plenty of water.

grammar.title: When / What should I …?
grammar.ar: لطلب النصيحة يمكن أن نبدأ بكلمة سؤال: When should we play? What should I take? والفعل بعد should يبقى في صورته الأساسية.
examples: When should we play? — In the evening.
What should I take? — Water and a cap.
Where should we sit? — In the shade.

words.ex: I exercise by riding my bike every afternoon.
Before a football match, you should warm up.
After running, I stretch my legs.
I'm out of breath after I run up the stairs.
When I'm tired, I take a break and drink some water.
After exercise, I feel full of energy and happy.

dialogue.t: I want to win the race. What should I do?
You should exercise every day.
Should I run very fast?
No, you shouldn't. Always warm up first.
What should I do when I'm out of breath?
You should take a break and drink some water.

grammar.title: should always / should never
grammar.ar: يمكن أن نضع always (دائماً) أو never (أبداً) بعد should: You should always warm up. You should never run after a big meal.
examples: You should always warm up first.
You should never exercise without water.
You should stretch after running.

words.ex: My best tip for a healthy life is to sleep well.
One of my healthy habits is walking to school.
I sometimes eat junk food when we go to the cinema.
To stay fit, I swim twice a week.
You should drink plenty of water when it's hot.
You should go to bed early before a big test.

dialogue.t: What's our first tip?
You should drink plenty of water.
And number two?
You shouldn't eat too much junk food.
What about sleep?
You should go to bed early on school nights.
Great poster!

grammar.title: Giving tips with reasons
grammar.ar: نبدأ كل نصيحة بـ You should أو You shouldn't + الفعل الأساسي، ونضيف السبب بـ because.
examples: You should drink plenty of water because it keeps you cool.
You shouldn't eat too much junk food because it isn't healthy.
You should exercise every day because it keeps you fit.
